descs.t: France riots: Macron vows strict action against the "sowers of chaos" as Paris activates a crisis unit amid nationwide protests. The historic town hall in Limoges collapsed after rioters set it on fire, crowds stormed City Hall in Marseille, and police in Paris came under attack. We go through the videos and posts from Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Limoges, in order.

Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Limoges: the France riots in one place. Macron promises order, his critics call for his resignation, and the footage shows town halls burning and police falling back. We look at what happened, who people on the ground blame, and what it means for the rest of Europe.

France is burning, and everyone is asking whether Macron has lost control. A 143-year-old town hall reduced to rubble, City Hall in Marseille stormed, police in Paris under attack. Many blame Islamism and the radical left. We show you the footage and you decide.

intro.plain: Welcome in. France is in chaos. Riots across Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Limoges, where the 143-year-old town hall collapsed after it was set on fire. descs.t: Trump and Russia sanctions: Rubio says Trump will take up to 60 days to weigh new sanctions, after an executive order waiving existing ones. Republican Rep. Don Bacon says he and other GOP lawmakers will push back, and the US has floated letting Russia sell more gas to Europe in a Ukraine peace deal. We go through every report and reaction.

Is the White House going soft on Putin? The sanctions waiver, the 60-day review, the gas offer to Europe and the Republican backlash, in one place. We look at what changed, who objects, and what it means for Ukraine.

Putin's war on Ukraine goes on, and Moscow still gets sanctions relief from Washington. Even Republicans like Don Bacon are pushing back. We show you every reaction and who really wins from this decision.
